rows.title: Did Treasury submit Scott Bessent's written answers from the September 15 HFSC hearing, which questions, answers or nonresponses became public, and did the packet disclose GOLD EAGLE's private participants or admission criteria?

badges.text: Past due, no record
No source link in the home

cells: Chairman Hill gave members five legislative days to submit additional written questions to the chair and asked Bessent to respond by October 20, 2026. At the September 17 check, House Event 119546 listed testimony, truth-in-testimony, biography, notice and memorandum, but no QFR packet or responses. Bessent described assistance by large banks and diffusion to smaller banks and service providers but named no fintech company, technology provider or blockchain network and supplied no GOLD EAGLE admission rule. Official launch materials identify participant classes but no complete private roster. Anthropic and Chainguard now supply named private support receipts, and Chainguard describes an Athena-to-Akrites-to-GOLD-EAGLE operating handoff, but those records do not establish formal GOLD EAGLE membership. Historical HFSC annual Treasury hearings have published written answers in the official GPO hearing volume, but the response due date is not a guaranteed public-posting date and a requested answer is not proof of timely or complete receipt. Look again when: On and after October 20, check House Event 119546 and HFSC Event 411218 for transmitted questions, response PDFs or a stated nonresponse; then check GovInfo for the eventual printed hearing record. First test whether the packet answers Huizenga's GOLD EAGLE question using the dedicated dossier's October inspection lens: roster and eligibility, exact operational roles, authority and liability, governance, technical carriage, maintainer/operator control, funding, performance, financial-system joins and the separate model-access boundary. Specifically compare any answer with the known Glasswing, Athena and Akrites rosters and Chainguard's September 15 operating account; do not convert membership in those programs into GOLD EAGLE admission. Use Ripple as the layer-1 stress test: distinguish Ripple Labs, Standard Custody, the proposed Ripple National Trust Bank, XRPL Foundation, validators and ecosystem maintainers; record whether any one is a finder, validator, CNA, maintainer, distributor, critical-infrastructure operator or recipient, and compare any claimed process with the February XRPL Batch vulnerability flow. Record whether 6 U.S.C. 1510 was extended or lapsed after September 30 without assuming GOLD EAGLE itself terminated. Also compare the packet with the four express in-hearing written-follow-up invitations concerning Trump Account escheat, an AI kill switch, TGA use for buybacks and SAR/CTR thresholds.

rows.title: What does the Supreme Court do with Custodia Bank's certiorari petition in No. 26-62, and what later account-access consequence follows?

badges.text: Dated
No source link in the home

cells: The petition was filed July 10 and docketed July 14. On October 13 the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City filed its brief in opposition. It argues there is no lower-court split, the Board's Payment Account proposal may reshape the dispute, Custodia's all-or-nothing mandamus case did not preserve an APA abuse-of-discretion or constitutional merits challenge, and sections 342 and 248a leave Reserve Banks at least some discretion. Only Kansas City's opposition was visible at the cutoff; no separate Board filing, Custodia reply, distribution, cert disposition, merits ruling or account change had posted. Look again when: Return earlier on a Board response or waiver, Custodia reply, Rule 15.5 waiting-period waiver or docketed distribution. Otherwise check the October 28 paid-list distribution; if distributed then, the published schedule points to the November 13 conference, subject to docket change. Continue through relist, order-list disposition, cert grant/denial, merits schedule or ruling, and any later Board/Reserve Bank/account-database action.

rows.title: What public legal design emerges from CFTC RIN 3038-AF80, Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets, after OIRA review?

badges.text: Condition
No source link in the home

cells: OIRA received AF80 on 2026-09-17 and concluded review on 2026-10-02 as Consistent with Change. On 2026-10-05 the CFTC announced an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking for Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (Regulation CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (Regulation CAM). The announcement confirms that CTXs are retail commodity transactions involving crypto assets under CEA section 2(c)(2)(D) and that CAM would be a purpose-built subcategory of designated contract market registration. It seeks input on abuse prevention, crypto-specific contextual guidance and best practices, and says comments will be due 60 days after Federal Register publication. As of the 2026-10-05 EDT cutoff, no AF80 text appears in the Federal Register or Public Inspection feeds, no document-specific Regulations.gov docket was reachable, and no question list, CFR text, exact authority analysis, Commission vote record, venue designation, listed CTX or operating market exists. The proposal advances a voluntary federal route for covered leveraged, margined or financed retail crypto transactions but does not give the CFTC power to require ordinary unleveraged spot crypto to trade on CFTC venues. Look again when: The AF80 ANPRM text, Federal Register notice or document-specific Regulations.gov docket appears; the comment period closes or is extended; the CFTC publishes an NPRM, final rule, vote record, legal analysis or updated actual-delivery interpretation; AF80 appears in the Unified Agenda; an official source links AF80 to AF66; or a named venue seeks or receives CAM designation and lists a CTX.

record.title: What first authoritative objects move either ARK's Exchange Class or Tokenized Class from exemptive permission into effective registration, venue admission, issuance, trading, settlement, accounting reconciliation and repeated operation?

badges.text: Dated
No source link in the home

cells: Order IC-36333 supplies immediately effective conditional exemptive permission for the architecture. As of September 30, no Tokenized Class registration, named blockchain, transfer agent/tokenization agent, wallet system, ATS, stablecoin rail, launch or transaction receipt was located. Class X registration effectiveness was delayed by Form 486BXT to October 23, 2026; intended TXSE listing and ticker ARKV do not yet establish admission or live trading. Look again when: Return earlier if ARK files a Tokenized Class registration statement or names its DLT, transfer-agent, wallet, ATS, cash or custody stack; if TXSE admits Class X or publishes a launch notice; or if an official filing, venue record, chain record, financial statement or auditor report evidences issuance, trade, settlement, repurchase, reconciliation or repeated operation.

record.title: Does XRP become recurring invisible bridge inventory rather than an optional protocol capability?

badges.text: Condition
No source link in the home

cells: October 14 targeted update: Evernorth identifies a 473 million XRP treasury and named Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo as execution partners, planning initial strategies in Q4 and later native lending when activated and proven. This establishes a substantial institutional capital supplier and intended deployment, but not deployed/borrowed amounts, recurring XRP payment intermediation or financed market-maker inventory economics. Ripple Prime collateral acceptance and BNY cash/custody relationships do not establish XRP or RLUSD use in FICC CIL. Prior route-level evidence limits remain; do not confuse treasury holdings with required operational inventory. Look again when: Ripple, a regulated liquidity provider, custodian, market maker or institutional customer publishes route-level XRP intermediation and inventory economics. Look for: Identify recurring permitted route share, unlike-asset or FX path, realized depth/slippage, gross and net inventory, borrowed amount, average holding time, turnover, financing cost, collateral haircut and hedge treatment. Evernorth publishes executed deployments and borrowers: distinguish lending/market-making demand from directional exposure and identify amount, duration, financing and hedge economics.
